contentHtml_en:
When you build an office suite, you picture a certain kind of user. A team in a meeting room. A student writing an essay. An accountant deep in a spreadsheet. And yes, those people use ONLYOFFICE every day.

But over 16 years, something wonderful happened. Our tools ended up in places we never planned for, helping people whose work looks nothing like a typical office. Firefighters. Human rights lawyers. Food bank volunteers. Even a skate park crew.

So let’s take a tour of the customers we didn’t expect. These are the stories that remind us why we do this.

When rescue workers need documents too

Firefighters run toward danger. We didn’t think document editing would be part of that job. We were wrong.

The Abensberg Fire Department in Germany uses ONLYOFFICE Docs together with Nextcloud to manage the paperwork behind the heroics. Duty rosters, equipment lists, training schedules, incident reports – all of it needs to be stored centrally and edited by the right people. Instead of juggling scattered files, the team shares and updates everything from one secure place. When a call comes in, the last thing anyone wants is to hunt for a document.

It turns out that saving lives involves a surprising amount of coordination behind the scenes. We’re glad our editors help keep that part running smoothly.

Open source for activists

Some of our most moving stories come from organizations fighting for people who need help.

Equal Rights Beyond Borders works on human rights and refugee law, often handling deeply confidential case files. They chose ONLYOFFICE precisely because they can control their own data. For an organization defending legal rights, keeping documents private isn’t a nice-to-have. It’s the whole point.

In Vietnam, the Blue Dragon Children’s Foundation uses ONLYOFFICE to support young people escaping trafficking and poverty. Their staff can focus on the mission instead of software licenses, working together on the documents that help vulnerable kids build safer futures.

These groups often run on tight budgets and even tighter privacy needs. Open-source, self-hosted tools give them power they couldn’t otherwise afford. That combination of freedom, security, and no cost barrier is exactly why they came to us.

Feeding people, one shared file at a time

Fighting hunger is logistics work. And logistics means documents.

The charitable foundation Food Bank used ONLYOFFICE to help coordinate a campaign that collected food worth 300,000 EUR. Behind that number are spreadsheets tracking donations, documents organizing volunteers, and plans keeping everyone aligned.

In Austria, Foodsharing Austria relies on ONLYOFFICE and Nextcloud to carry out a mission built entirely on sharing, namely rescuing surplus food before it goes to waste. And the Vegan in Leipzig project uses the same combination to keep its community workflows running smoothly.

None of these teams set out to become power users of an office suite. They just needed reliable tools that wouldn’t get in the way of doing good.

The places no one expected

Here’s where things get delightfully unusual.

A skate park. Yes, really. St. Skatepark Zuidlaren in the Netherlands uses ONLYOFFICE to organize its local spot for sports and community activities. Planning sessions, events, and coordination, all handled with the same editors a corporation might use for quarterly reports.

Then there’s the internet. An entire online meme community, GoodAnimemes, turned to ONLYOFFICE to keep its document workflows secure. Memes may be for fun, but running a large community still takes real organization.

Music lovers are covered too. ONLYOFFICE has helped organize music festivals in Germany, wrangling the countless schedules, contracts, and logistics that go into a live event. A sports society leaned on ONLYOFFICE to push through the challenges of the pandemic and keep its members connected.

Image source: u-run.fr

And let’s not forget the youth football club that used ONLYOFFICE to coordinate a distributed team of volunteer managers. Anyone who has tried to organize a group of volunteers knows it can feel harder than winning the match itself.

Serving whole cities and countries

Sometimes “unexpected” simply means far-reaching.

In Laos, government officials edit and collaborate on documents through ONLYOFFICE Docs, powering everyday administrative work at a national level. Across the Pacific, the University of French Polynesia made seamless online collaboration a reality for staff and students on a group of islands in the middle of the ocean.

Closer to some of our readers, the city of Hopewell, Virginia adopted ONLYOFFICE to enable remote work for 500 government employees when they suddenly needed it most.

And in Spain, the city council of Reus brought simple, powerful online editing to its public administration.

The city hall of Reus (The image by Josep Llauradó is licensed under CC BY-SA 2.1 ES)

From a small skate park to a national government, the same tools scale to fit. That flexibility is something we’re quietly proud of.

What all these stories have in common

Look closely, and a pattern appears. Fire departments, activists, food banks, festivals, city halls. None of them are “typical” office users. Yet they all needed the same core things:

  • control over their data, especially when handling sensitive or confidential information;
  • tools that fit their budget, whether they’re a global institution or a volunteer group;
  • the freedom of open source, with no lock-in and no compromises;
  • real collaboration that works across distances, devices, and teams.

That’s the quiet magic of building something open and universal. You create a tool for “everyone,” and then everyone shows up, including people you never pictured.

Built for everyone means everyone

When we started, our mission was simple: bring the most innovative office apps to everyone. We meant it as a promise. We didn’t fully grasp just how wide “everyone” would turn out to be.

Today, more than 21 million people use ONLYOFFICE. Some of them are exactly who we expected. Many of them are not, and those are the stories that make us smile the most. A firefighter updating a roster. A lawyer protecting a refugee’s case file. A volunteer sorting donated food. A skater planning the next event.

Each one proves the same point: good tools should serve any mission, big or small, ordinary or extraordinary.

So here’s our question for you: are you one of the customers we didn’t expect?

If ONLYOFFICE plays a surprising role in your work, community, or cause, we’d love to hear about it. You might just become our next favorite example of what “for everyone” really means. Tell us your story

author: Sergey
contentHtml:
Summary

The ONLYOFFICE connector v2.1.0 for Confluence Cloud introduces several enhancements, including support for more file formats, a dedicated space page for easier access to attachments, and improved file browsing features. Users can now navigate documents more efficiently and manage attachments with greater ease, all while benefiting from a new demo server for testing purposes.

  • New supported formats include Apple iWork and Hancom Office.
  • A dedicated space page simplifies access to attachments.
  • Improved file browsing features enhance navigation.
  • Users can manage attachments through a content tree.
  • A demo server is available for 30 days.

The latest version of the ONLYOFFICE connector for Confluence Cloud brings some important updates to Confluence users, allowing them to work with more file formats, access all attachments in a dedicated space and look through documents with ease. Read this post to learn all the details.

New supported formats

The updated ONLYOFFICE connector for Confluence Cloud significantly expands the list of supported file formats. For example, you can now work with the following:

  • Apple iWork formats: Pages, Keynote, Numbers;
  • Hancom Office formats: HWP, HWPX;
  • MD documents;
  • ODG presentations;
  • VSDX, VSSX, VSTX, VSDM, VSSM and VSTM diagrams.

Dedicated ONLYOFFICE space page

The updated connector creates a dedicated workspace where you can access all Confluence pages, blog posts and attachments. This means that you no longer need to open a specific page to be able to edit its attachments. Everything is accessible in one place, so you can easily navigate through pages and files and find what you need in seconds.

The ONLYOFFICE space also allows you to create new files on any page, using the Create button.

To access the space, simply click the ONLYOFFICE icon on the left-side panel.

Improved file browsing

The ONLYOFFICE space comes with improved file browsing, which makes it easier to look through files and attachments. Equipped with a localized UI, it provides a search bar, filtering and sorting tools, and support for breadcrumbs and pagination. All these features are designed to make file navigation a breeze.

Content tree actions for attachments

With the updated ONLYOFFICE connector, attachment management has become easier. You can now easily open, download and delete attachments using a content tree with the corresponding options. To access it, click the three-dot icon of the required file.

Access to a demo server

The ONLYOFFICE connector v2.1.0 Confluence Cloud introduces a redesigned settings page where you can enter the parameters of your ONLYOFFICE Docs instance or connect to a demo server. The demo server gives you an opportunity to try the integration without having to deploy an ONLYOFFICE Docs instance.

Note: The demo server is available for 30 days and is not recommended for sensitive data and confidential files.

Migration from Atlassian Connect to Forge

One more improvement that might go unnoticed but is worth a mention is the migration from Atlassian Connect to Forge, a serverless, Atlassian-hosted architecture. Since the ONLYOFFICE connector for Confluence Cloud is now a Forge app, Atlassian takes care of hosting, scaling and monitoring its code. This allows us to focus on building new functionality for the app rather than worrying about its deployments. Another good thing about this migration is that we can provide a custom UI for our app.

Other improvements

What else is new in the ONLYOFFICE connector v2.1.0 Confluence Cloud:

  • new empty file templates;
  • support for opening referenced documents from the editors;
  • several error fixes.

Find the full changelog on GitHub.

Get ONLYOFFICE

Get the latest version of the ONLYOFFICE connector for Confluence Cloud from the Atlassian Marketplace:

GET THE APP

FAQ: ONLYOFFICE connector for Confluence Cloud

Question: What is the ONLYOFFICE connector for Confluence Cloud?

The ONLYOFFICE connector enables users to edit and collaborate on office files directly within Confluence Cloud, a web-based productivity platform developed by Atlassian.

Question: Is the ONLYOFFICE connector for Confluence Cloud free?

Yes, the app is free. You can install it from the Atlassian Marketplace.

Question: Is the connector compatible with Confluence Data Center?

If you use Confluence Data Center, you can get the corresponding ONLYOFFICE app from Atlassian Marketplace.

Question: Do I need to install anything to use the integration?

Yes, you do. You need to deploy ONLYOFFICE Docs on-premises or sign up for the cloud-based version.

Question: How do I test the integration before implementing it?

For testing purposes, you can install the ONLYOFFICE connector and connect to a demo ONLYOFFICE Docs server. It’s a public test server available for 30 days, which allows you to check the functionality of the ONLYOFFICE editors before full implementation.

author: Sergey
contentHtml:
Summary

The latest updates to the ONLYOFFICE connectors for Odoo introduce several enhancements, including the ability to open PDFs directly from preview mode, create documents from form templates, and improvements to the Templates module. These features streamline document management and editing processes, making it easier for users to work with PDFs and templates within the Odoo platform.

  • Open PDFs directly from preview mode.
  • Create documents from PDF form templates.
  • Save completed forms to the Documents module.
  • Convert PDF files to fillable forms.
  • View templates as a list for easier navigation.

Great news for Odoo users!

The official ONLYOFFICE connectors for Odoo, including the core integration apps for the Enterprise and Community versions of the open-source ERP platform, and the Templates app, have been updated. The new releases make it easier to open PDFs and create documents from form templates, and improve the Templates module overall.

Read this blog post to discover what’s new in each integration app.

Odoo Enterprise: what’s new

The ONLYOFFICE connector for the Enterprise edition of the ERP platform has received several improvements. Let’s take a look at them.

Open PDFs from preview mode

The updated connector for Odoo Enterprise makes it easier to work with PDF files in the Documents module, allowing you to open them directly from preview mode. When you open a PDF file in preview mode, you just need to click the Open in ONLYOFFICE button in the upper right corner for further editing in another tab.

Create documents from form templates

Another improvement for the Documents module within the Odoo platform lets you create new documents directly from PDF form templates. When creating a new document by clicking the New button in the upper left corner and choosing Create with ONLYOFFICE, you will be offered to select one of the following options:

  • Blank
  • From Template

The latter is what allows you to access the built-in gallery of templates, which includes documents, spreadsheets, presentations and PDF forms. Choose the PDF form you need, open it and edit it the way you like.

Create, upload and move documents within system folders

The updated ONLYOFFICE connector also makes document management within the module easier, allowing you to create and upload documents to system folders (My Drive, Company, etc.). Additionally, now you can move documents, spreadsheets, presentations and PDFs between directories.

Opening folders shared via a link

File sharing is another aspect improved by the newest version of the ONLYOFFICE integration app. Now you can share not only separate files via a link but whole folders. External users can open shared folders in their browser and either open files in the ONLYOFFICE editors or download them to their device.

What’s next: work with Odoo documents via ONLYOFFICE Desktop Editors

One of the most useful improvements of the version 6.3.1 release is the ability to connect your Odoo account to ONLYOFFICE Desktop Editors. This way, you can access your documents via the desktop app and edit them using local system fonts, the clipboard and system printers, available on your OS.

Note: Although this integration is already enabled, the corresponding option will be available in the desktop application for Windows, Linux and macOS in the next release. Stay tuned!

GET THE APP

Odoo Community: open TSV files

The ONLYOFFICE connector for the Community edition of the Odoo ERP platform has also been improved. The most important update is support for TSV (Tab-Separated Values) files. Now you can open such files attached to the Sales, Invoicing and other Odoo modules, using the Open in ONLYOFFICE option.

The updated integration app also comes with a lot of bug fixes and removes the outdated methods.

GET THE APP

ONLYOFFICE Templates app: what’s new

The ONLYOFFICE Templates app for Odoo brings some useful improvements to the corresponding module. Let’s find out what’s new in this release.

Save completed forms to the Documents module

Another important improvement in the ONLYOFFICE Templates app is the ability to save forms with completed fields directly to the Documents module. Now you can open ONLYOFFICE templates in the required module (for example, Sales or Invoicing) and save them to a specific folder, using the Add to Documents option.

After saving, your template will be available in the selected location within the Documents module. Now you can share it with other Odoo users and collaborate in real time.

Convert PDF files to forms

When creating or modifying a template within the Templates module, you can now convert PDF files to forms with fillable fields. This means that you don’t have to create templates from scratch. You can simply upload a PDF file and turn it into a fillable PDF form, using ONLYOFFICE Form Creator.

View templates as a list

With the latest update, viewing templates has become much easier. In addition to the Kanban style mode, now you can view templates as a list if you enable the corresponding option in the upper right corner, right under your user profile.

Navigate among Odoo fields with ease

Since Odoo provides plenty of fields that you can choose from when creating your templates, navigating among them might be time-consuming. However, this is no longer a problem with the updated ONLYOFFICE templates app. Now you can simply click on a field in your ONLYOFFICE template, and you will automatically scroll to the corresponding Odoo field on the left-side panel. This way, you can access the desired fields much quicker.

GET THE APP

Get started with the ONLYOFFICE and Odoo integration

Want to know how to connect your Odoo platform with the ONLYOFFICE editors to be able to create, edit and collaborate on documents, spreadsheets, presentations and PDFs directly within your business environment? Watch the video below:

FAQ: ONLYOFFICE and Odoo integration

How many ONLYOFFICE connectors are there for Odoo?

We offer three official modules for Odoo:

  • ONLYOFFICE is a main module compatible with Odoo Community. It allows you to open and edit office files attached to various modules (Sales, Invoicing, Calendar, etc.), and its installation is required for other ONLYOFFICE connectors to work.
  • ONLYOFFICE Documents is a module used for creating, editing and collaborating on office files within the Documents module in Odoo Enterprise.
  • ONLYOFFICE Templates is a module used for creating and editing fillable forms within a separate module. It requires ONLYOFFICE Automation API.

Do I need to install ONLYOFFICE Docs to use this integration?

Yes. To make this integration work, you need to have an ONLYOFFICE Docs instance deployed locally or in the cloud, and connected to your Odoo platform via the integration apps.

Can I try this integration before its implementation?

Sure. You can connect a public ONLYOFFICE Docs test server on the settings page and see how it works for you.

Where do I find guides for the ONLYOFFICE and Odoo integration?

You can take a look at our Help Center and API documentation.

How do I request a new feature for this integration?

You can share your ideas and request new features in our community.

author: Serge
contentHtml:
Want to see how online document editing could work in your own application? A working example makes the first steps easier. ONLYOFFICE Create App gives you that starting point. It generates a small web application with a file manager and the code needed to connect ONLYOFFICE Docs. Once you configure access to a running Docs instance, you can try the editor in your browser and explore the project at your own pace.

Meet ONLYOFFICE Create App

Available on npm, ONLYOFFICE Create App is a command-line tool that creates a sample integration project.

The generated app uses Next.js and React. It includes a file manager where you can upload files or create new documents, spreadsheets, presentations and PDF forms. It also provides an editor page and the server code that handles document downloads and saving.

There are two crucial components of the app:

  • Create App prepares the website.
  • ONLYOFFICE Docs provides the document editors.

Note! ONLYOFFICE Docs are installed and connected separately. The npm command does not install Document Server or launch Docker for you.

Prerequisites

  • Node.js 20.12 or later
  • ONLYOFFICE Docs 8.2 or later
  • npm package manager and stable internet connection

For the walkthrough below, we use Windows PowerShell and assume that ONLYOFFICE Docs is already running in Docker Desktop on port 80. If you have not installed Docs yet, follow the Docker installation guide first.

Docker is one way to run Docs locally. It is not required on your computer when you connect to an existing server elsewhere.

Create your first application

  1. Open PowerShell in the folder where you want to keep the project. Then run: 
    npx @onlyoffice/create-app my-docs-app

    If npm asks whether to install the generator, confirm with y. The command creates a folder called my-docs-app and installs the application’s dependencies.

  2. Wait for the installation to finish, then move into the new folder: 
    cd my-docs-app

    Note! Commands that start the app must run in its project folder, where package.json is located. Running npm install in an unrelated empty folder will not create an ONLYOFFICE integration.

Connect the app to ONLYOFFICE Docs

For this local Docker Desktop setup, edit these entries in env .and leave the other generated settings in place:

DOCUMENT_SERVER_URL=http://localhost:80
DOCUMENT_SERVER_JWT_SECRET=your_actual_docs_secret
APP_URL=http://your_local_ip_adress:3000

DOCUMENT_SERVER_URL tells the browser where to find the editors. APP_URL tells Docs where to download your files and send saved changes. Here, host.docker.internal lets the container reach the application running on Windows. We use port 3000 for the app so it can run alongside another example on port 3000.

DOCUMENT_SERVER_JWT_SECRET is a shared secret used to verify requests between the two components. Replace the example text with the actual secret configured for your Docs instance. When editing .env manually, paste the value itself. For Docker installations, set the secret with the container environment variable JWT_SECRET and use the same value for DOCUMENT_SERVER_JWT_SECRET in the app.

APP_URL: Replace your_local_ip_adress with your computer’s local IP address, reachable from the Docs container.

For this Docker setup, Docs must also be allowed to request files from the host’s private address. Our test container used ALLOW_PRIVATE_IP_ADDRESS=true, an option described in the official Docker image documentation.

Open the app in your browser

Save .env and start the application:

npm start

In this template, the start command downloads the blank document templates, builds the application and launches the web server. You do not need a separate build command for this first run.

Once the server is ready, open http:///your_local_ip_adress:3000. Keep the terminal running while you use the app.

You will see a file manager with a README sample. You can create other documents. ONLYOFFICE Docs will load inside the application, ready for you to try editing.

Try your own integration

Create App gives you a practical way to get familiar with ONLYOFFICE Docs integration. You can start with a small working example, see how a document moves through the editing and saving process, and use that understanding when building your own application.

Explore the Create App repository on GitHub, generate your first project and open a document in your browser. For a closer look at the integration options, continue with the ONLYOFFICE Docs API documentation. Have an idea or suggestion? Open an issue on GitHub or email us.

FAQ: ONLYOFFICE Create App

Does Create App install ONLYOFFICE Docs?

No. It creates a small web application with a file manager and the code that facilitates the connection to ONLYOFFICE Docs. Install ONLYOFFICE Docs separately or connect an existing instance.

Is Docker required?

Only if you choose to run Docs in Docker. There are several options for deploying ONLYOFFICE Docs, including Ubuntu, CentOS, Windows Server, and Amazon Machine Images. You can also use an existing Docs server.

Can I adapt the app for my own project?

Yes. You can modify the generated code. See the ONLYOFFICE Docs API documentation for integration details.

author: Dasha
contentHtml:
Summary

Fleurdelix OS has chosen ONLYOFFICE as its default office suite to provide users with a modern, open-source solution that supports familiar file formats like DOCX, XLSX, and PPTX. This choice aligns with Fleurdelix's mission of digital sovereignty and data control, allowing organizations to work seamlessly with documents without relying on external cloud providers. The integration with Nextcloud further enhances collaboration and file management within the Fleurdelix ecosystem.

  • Fleurdelix OS focuses on digital sovereignty and data control.
  • ONLYOFFICE supports familiar file formats for easy document handling.
  • Integration with Nextcloud enhances collaboration capabilities.
  • The suite is preinstalled, requiring no additional setup.
  • It is designed for organizations with high-security requirements.

We continue our series on operating systems that set ONLYOFFICE Desktop Editors as their default office suite. This time, we take a look at Fleurdelix OS, a free operating system focused on digital sovereignty, data control, and open source technologies.

Who is Fleurdelix OS for, what problem does it aim to solve, and why did its team choose ONLYOFFICE as a default office suite? Discover in the blog post below.

A free and sovereign operating system

Fleurdelix OS is a free, sovereign operating system with built-in AI built by design. It runs on PCs, Macs, virtual machines, Docker containers, and sovereign private clouds.

The goal is to give organizations full control over their infrastructure and data, without depending on foreign cloud providers or recurring license fees.

Fleurdelix is designed for organizations with high-level security, compliance, and data control requirements, including those in healthcare, aerospace, finance, manufacturing, real-time systems, and business management. More broadly, the system is designed for public and private organizations looking for an alternative to proprietary ecosystems.

Fleurdelix OS is based on Ubuntu Server 26.04 Minimal. The team integrates open source components such as Nextcloud for file management and collaboration, and ONLYOFFICE for working with office documents.

Why Fleurdelix chose ONLYOFFICE

ONLYOFFICE Desktop Editors is preinstalled on Fleurdelix OS, giving users tools for documents, spreadsheets, presentations, and PDFs with no additional installation.

The Fleurdelix team was looking for an open source office suite that supports familiar file formats and lets users continue working with documents created in Microsoft Office. ONLYOFFICE supports formats such as DOCX, XLSX, and PPTX, so users can avoid unnecessary conversions when exchanging files.

The integration with Nextcloud was another factor in the decision. Nextcloud is already part of the Fleurdelix ecosystem, making it possible to combine file management and collaboration with ONLYOFFICE document editing.

Other features of Desktop Editors:

  • PDF editor for editing, annotating, and redacting PDFs.
  • Form creator to build fillable questionnaires, queries, and administrative documents.
  • Plugins to extend the editors with additional tools and services to fit their workflows.
  • Built-in template library to use ready-made documents for your needs.
  • AI tools to work faster and choose different AI providers, even locally hosted models, giving organizations more flexibility and control over how AI is used with their documents.

For Fleurdelix, choosing an office suite was part of building a complete sovereign environment rather than simply adding another application to the operating system.

Dominique, CEO of Fleurdelix:

Digital sovereignty is not only about where data is stored. It’s also about giving people tools they can actually work with every day. ONLYOFFICE gave us exactly that: a modern, open source office suite with outstanding Microsoft compatibility that fits naturally into our sovereign ecosystem alongside Nextcloud.

Get ONLYOFFICE Desktop Editors

ONLYOFFICE Desktop Editors is available for Windows, Linux, and macOS. The free desktop suite lets users work locally with documents, spreadsheets, presentations, and PDFs.

Summary

Cloud-based productivity apps are essential tools that help teams manage documents, deadlines, and communication efficiently across various projects. These applications enable real-time collaboration and shared access to files and tasks, making them ideal for both office-based and remote teams. The guide highlights 20 of the best cloud-based productivity apps, covering their features, pricing, and suitability for different team needs.

Managing documents, deadlines, and team communication across several projects can quickly become complicated. Cloud-based productivity apps help keep everything organized, giving colleagues shared access to files, tasks, and conversations wherever they work.

This guide covers 20 productivity tools for document editing, project management, communication, scheduling, and more. Explore their key features, pricing, advantages, and limitations to find the right fit for your team.

What are cloud-based productivity apps?

Cloud-based productivity apps let people create documents, manage tasks, and share information online. Unlike traditional desktop software that relies mainly on locally stored files, these tools make shared content accessible across devices and allow colleagues to work together in real time.

They are used by both office-based and remote teams, with features ranging from collaborative editing and file storage to project tracking and online meetings.

Types of cloud-based productivity apps

Different applications serve different purposes. The table below provides an overview of the main categories and the tools covered in this guide.

Category Apps
Cloud office suites ONLYOFFICE, Google Workspace, Microsoft 365
Project and task management Asana, Trello, ClickUp
Team communication Slack, Microsoft Teams, Mattermost
Video conferencing Zoom, Google Meet, Webex
Cloud storage Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive
Time management Toggl Track, Clockify, Calendly
AI productivity tools ChatGPT, Notion AI

Cloud office suites and document collaboration

Cloud office suites let colleagues create and review documents together, with shared editing, comments, and file management features.

1. ONLYOFFICE

ONLYOFFICE provides a full set of editors for documents, spreadsheets, presentations, PDFs, and fillable forms, giving teams everything they need to work with office files in one place. Users can co-edit documents in real time, leave comments, and track changes, making collaboration easier and more transparent. In addition to editing tools, ONLYOFFICE offers a shared workspace where teams can organize documents into rooms and manage access permissions securely.

Support for popular Microsoft Office formats makes it easier to exchange files with clients, partners, and other external stakeholders without compatibility concerns. The World Food Travel Association, for example, uses ONLYOFFICE to collaborate effectively across multiple time zones and engage volunteers in its projects.

CREATE FREE CLOUD

Pros: Collaborative editing, Office format compatibility, flexible sharing permissions, cloud or self-hosted deployment.

Cons: Project scheduling and team messaging require separate tools.

Pricing: The Cloud Startup plan is free. The Business plan is currently available at a rate of $20 per admin per month.

Best for: Teams working with Office documents and businesses regularly collaborating with external partners.

2. Google Workspace

Google Workspace brings Docs, Sheets, Slides, Gmail, Drive, and Calendar into one connected environment. Several colleagues can edit the same document, discuss changes in comments, and access the latest version without exchanging email attachments.

The applications work primarily in a browser, although complex Microsoft Office files may need formatting adjustments when opened in Google’s editors.

Pros: Real-time collaboration, simple file sharing, and integration across Google services.

Cons: Advanced spreadsheet features and complex Office formatting may not transfer perfectly between applications.

Pricing: Business Starter costs $7 per user per month with annual commitment; Business Standard costs $14.

Best for: Teams that regularly collaborate on documents and already use Google’s business applications.

3. Microsoft 365

Microsoft 365 combines Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook with online storage and collaboration services. Its desktop applications remain useful for detailed spreadsheets, complex documents, and presentations requiring precise formatting.

Employees can work locally or online and share files through Microsoft cloud services. Businesses should review the available subscriptions carefully, as desktop applications, Teams, and other services are not included in every package.

Pros: Advanced Office applications, desktop and online editing, and integrated business services.

Cons: Multiple subscription options and additional administration for larger deployments.

Pricing: Business Basic with Teams starts at $7 per user per month with annual billing. Business Standard, which includes desktop Office applications, starts at $14.

Best for: Businesses already using Microsoft products and teams working extensively with Office documents.

Project and task management

A task manager gives everyone a clearer picture of their responsibilities, upcoming deadlines, and the progress of shared projects.

4. Asana

Asana helps teams coordinate assignments through lists, boards, calendars, and timelines. Tasks can include deadlines, comments, attachments, and dependencies, making it easier to follow work involving several contributors.

Marketing and operations teams can use Asana to keep projects moving between departments, with additional reporting and resource management features available on higher-tier plans.

Pros: Clear task ownership, multiple project views, and cross-team coordination.

Cons: Portfolio and workload management require more expensive subscriptions.

Pricing: Personal is free for up to two users. Starter costs $10.99 per user per month with annual billing.

Best for: Teams managing projects with multiple contributors and approval stages.

5. Trello

Trello uses visual boards to organize work into lists and cards. An editorial team, for example, can move articles from writing to editing and publication, with deadlines, checklists, and supporting files attached to each card.

The interface is easy to learn and works particularly well for projects with clearly defined stages. More complicated schedules and task dependencies may call for additional project management features.

Pros: Easy setup, customizable boards, and visual progress tracking.

Cons: Limited advanced scheduling and reporting compared with more comprehensive project management platforms.

Image source: Trello

Pricing: A free plan is available. Standard costs $5 per user per month with annual billing; Premium costs $10.

Best for: Small teams, editorial calendars, and straightforward project workflows.

6. ClickUp

ClickUp combines task management with documents, dashboards, time tracking, and workflow automation. Agencies can use it to organize several client projects, keeping assignments and supporting materials in the same workspace.

Teams can customize project views and task statuses, but that flexibility also requires some planning. An overly complicated workspace may become difficult to maintain as more people and projects are added.

Pros: Customizable workflows, multiple project views, and integrated documents.

Cons: More configuration is needed than with a simple task management app.

Pricing: Free Forever is available. Unlimited starts at $7 per user per month with annual billing.

Best for: Agencies and growing teams managing several projects simultaneously.

Team communication

Team communication apps provide a shared space for everyday discussions, project updates, and quick questions that do not require a formal meeting.

7. Slack

Slack keeps conversations organized in channels dedicated to projects, departments, or specific topics. Employees can share files, exchange messages, and receive updates from connected business applications.

Its extensive integrations make it convenient for teams working across several platforms. However, important decisions can get lost when discussions are spread across too many channels.

Pros: Organized messaging, integrations with other tools, and collaboration with external partners.

Cons: Excessive notifications and lengthy message threads can make information harder to follow.

Image source: Slack

Pricing: A free plan is available. Pro costs $7.25 per active user per month with annual billing.

Best for: Remote teams and businesses using several specialized applications.

8. Microsoft Teams

Microsoft Teams brings messaging, meetings, and file sharing together. Employees using Microsoft 365 can discuss projects in dedicated channels and open shared Office documents directly from their workspace.

Teams is a convenient choice for organizations already working within Microsoft’s ecosystem. As the number of projects grows, consistent channel organization becomes important for keeping conversations and documents easy to find.

Pros: Integrated messaging, meetings, and document collaboration.

Cons: Conversations and files can become scattered across chats and channels.

Pricing: Teams Essentials starts at $4 per user per month with annual billing. Teams is also included in eligible Microsoft 365 subscriptions.

Best for: Organizations using Microsoft 365 and teams combining office-based and remote work.

9. Mattermost

Mattermost provides channel-based messaging and file sharing, with the option to run the platform on an organization’s own infrastructure.

Its deployment flexibility appeals to development teams and IT departments that need greater control over their communication environment. Self-hosting, however, requires technical resources for installation, updates, and maintenance.

Pros: Flexible hosting, organized communication, and support for technical workflows.

Cons: Self-hosted deployments require ongoing administration.

Pricing: A free, open-source Team Edition is available for self-hosting. Commercial Professional and Enterprise plans require a sales quotation.

Best for: Development teams, IT departments, and organizations with specific hosting requirements.

Video conferencing and online meetings

Video conferencing tools are used for everything from short team calls to training sessions and virtual events. Meeting duration, participant limits, and compatibility with existing calendars are worth checking before choosing a platform.

10. Zoom

Zoom supports video meetings, webinars, and virtual workshops. Screen sharing and breakout rooms let participants present information, hold smaller discussions, and return to the main meeting afterward.

Zoom Workplace also includes messaging and collaborative features. Businesses planning longer sessions should consider a paid plan, as free group meetings have a time limit.

Pros: Flexible meeting formats, breakout rooms, and screen sharing.

Cons: Free group meetings are limited to 40 minutes.

Image source: Zoom

Pricing: Zoom Workplace Basic is free. Pro is listed at $15.99 per user per month with monthly billing.

Best for: Client meetings, online training, and virtual workshops.

11. Google Meet

Google Meet works with Google Calendar and other Workspace applications, making it easy to schedule and join meetings directly from a browser. Participants can share their screens and join calls without installing additional desktop software.

The free version covers basic meetings, while recording and other advanced features are available through eligible Google Workspace subscriptions.

Pros: Browser-based access and integration with Google Calendar.

Cons: Free group meetings are limited to 60 minutes.

Pricing: A free version is available. Additional business features are included in eligible Google Workspace plans, starting at $7 per user per month with annual commitment.

Best for: Small businesses and teams already using Google Workspace.

12. Webex

Webex by Cisco offers video meetings, messaging, and screen sharing. Businesses with compatible Cisco meeting room equipment can connect employees attending from the office with colleagues joining remotely.

The platform also supports more extensive communication requirements, although its different meeting and calling products have separate licensing options.

Pros: Hybrid meeting support and integration with Cisco equipment.

Cons: Selecting the appropriate plan requires comparing different communication and meeting products.

Pricing: Webex Free supports meetings lasting up to 40 minutes. Webex Meet starts at $12 per user per month with annual billing.

Best for: Hybrid organizations and businesses using Cisco collaboration systems.

Cloud storage and file sharing

Cloud storage keeps documents and other business files accessible across devices. When comparing services, consider how files are synchronized, who can access them, and whether storage is already included in your office software.

13. Google Drive

Google Drive stores documents, spreadsheets, images, and other files online. Employees can share folders, manage access permissions, and open compatible files directly in Google Workspace.

Business subscriptions also provide shared drives, allowing project files to remain available to the team rather than being stored exclusively in an individual employee’s account.

Pros: Easy sharing, collaborative editing, and shared team storage.

Cons: Storage is shared across Google services, and external sharing permissions need careful management.

Pricing: Personal accounts include 15 GB of free storage. Workspace Business Starter provides 30 GB of pooled storage per user for $7 per user per month with annual commitment.

Best for: Teams working extensively with Google documents.

14. Dropbox

Dropbox synchronizes files across devices and makes it easy to share materials with colleagues or clients. Its desktop application works with familiar folders, so employees can continue managing files without changing how they normally navigate their computers.

Creative agencies can use Dropbox to exchange large design files and media assets, although editing Office documents and managing complex projects may require separate applications.

Pros: Cross-device synchronization, convenient file sharing, and large file transfers.

Cons: Limited free storage and fewer native office editing features than dedicated office suites.

Pricing: Dropbox Basic is free with 2 GB of storage. Standard costs $15 per user per month.

Best for: Creative agencies and businesses regularly exchanging large files.

15. OneDrive

OneDrive integrates cloud storage with Windows and Microsoft 365. Employees can synchronize files across devices, share documents, and open compatible files in Office applications.

OneDrive is generally used for files associated with individual employees, while SharePoint provides shared document libraries for departments and project teams.

Pros: Windows integration, file synchronization, and Office collaboration.

Cons: Teams need clear guidelines for organizing files between OneDrive and SharePoint.

Pricing: OneDrive is included in Microsoft 365 Business Basic, starting at $7 per user per month with annual billing and providing 1 TB of cloud storage per user.

Best for: Businesses already using Microsoft 365.

Time management, scheduling and time tracking

Time management apps help businesses record working hours, review project costs, and arrange appointments. The tools below cover two distinct needs: tracking time spent on work and finding suitable meeting times.

16. Toggl Track

Toggl Track records time spent on tasks, projects, and client assignments. Employees can start a timer or enter hours manually, while reports help businesses review billable work and prepare more accurate project estimates.

Pros: Simple time recording, project reports, and billable time tracking.

Cons: Advanced reporting and team management features require paid subscriptions.

Image source: Toggle Track

Pricing: A free plan is available. Starter costs $9 per user per month with annual billing.

Best for: Freelancers, consultants, and agencies tracking billable hours.

17. Clockify

Clockify combines time tracking with timesheets and project reporting. Employees record their hours against individual activities, giving managers a clearer picture of the time spent on different assignments.

Paid plans extend these features with invoicing, timesheet approvals, and additional administration options.

Pros: Free time tracking, timesheets, and project reports.

Cons: Invoicing and timesheet approvals require paid plans.

Pricing: A free plan is available. Basic starts at $3.99 per seat per month with annual billing.

Best for: Small businesses and teams that need detailed timesheets.

18. Calendly

Calendly takes the back-and-forth out of appointment scheduling. Users share a booking link, and clients or colleagues select a time based on their availability and connected calendars.

Recruiters, consultants, and sales teams can use it to arrange interviews, consultations, and product demonstrations. Paid subscriptions add more advanced scheduling options for teams.

Pros: Automated booking, calendar integrations, and meeting reminders.

Cons: Multiple event types and advanced team scheduling require a paid plan.

Pricing: A free plan is available. Standard starts at $10 per seat per month with annual billing.

Best for: Recruiters, consultants, and sales teams arranging frequent appointments.

AI productivity tools

AI tools can assist with writing, research, and information retrieval. Some work as standalone assistants, while others use content already stored in an organization’s collaborative workspace.

19. ChatGPT

ChatGPT can help employees prepare content outlines, summarize reports, analyze data, and draft internal documents. Its range of capabilities makes it useful across different departments, from marketing and research to software development.

AI-generated information should still be checked before being used in professional materials. Businesses also need appropriate privacy settings when working with confidential information.

Pros: Assistance with writing, research, analysis, and document preparation.

Cons: Generated information requires verification, and confidential data needs appropriate privacy controls.

Pricing: A free plan is available. ChatGPT Business Standard seats start at $20 per user per month with annual billing.

Best for: Marketing teams, researchers, analysts, and other knowledge workers.

20. Notion AI

Notion AI adds AI-assisted writing, summarization, and search to Notion’s collaborative workspace. Teams can retrieve information from their existing project plans, meeting notes, and internal documentation without switching to another application.

Its value depends on the quality of the material stored in Notion, making consistent documentation important for reliable information retrieval.

Pros: Document summarization, knowledge retrieval, and AI assistance within an existing workspace.

Cons: An organized knowledge base and an eligible subscription are needed to make full use of its capabilities.

Image source: Notion

Pricing: Notion offers a free plan with limited AI access. Its Business subscription includes expanded AI capabilities, with pricing depending on the billing option and region.

Best for: Teams managing internal documentation and shared knowledge in Notion.

How to choose a cloud-based productivity app

Begin with the tasks that take up most of your team’s time. A business handling contracts and reports may need an office suite with reliable document compatibility, while an agency managing several client projects may benefit more from dedicated task management software.

Check your existing subscriptions before adding new applications. Google Workspace and Microsoft 365, for example, already include document editing, storage, and video conferencing. You may not need a separate tool for every activity.

Costs should be assessed across the whole team, including storage, administration features, and access for external collaborators. Review security and sharing permissions as well, particularly when employees work with confidential documents.

Before committing to a platform, test it with a real project. Involve the employees who will use it regularly and see how easily they can find information, complete assignments, and work together.

Conclusion

Cloud-based productivity apps help teams manage documents, projects, communication, and other everyday activities. Choosing the right combination starts with understanding your team’s needs and making use of the software you already have.

A few well-chosen tools can provide everything a team needs without adding unnecessary complexity or extra subscriptions.

Time management Toggl Track, Clockify, Calendly
AI productivity tools ChatGPT, Notion AI

Cloud office suites and document collaboration

Cloud office suites let colleagues create and review documents together, with shared editing, comments, and file management features.

1. ONLYOFFICE

ONLYOFFICE provides a full set of editors for documents, spreadsheets, presentations, PDFs, and fillable forms, giving teams everything they need to work with office files in one place. Users can co-edit documents in real time, leave comments, and track changes, making collaboration easier and more transparent. In addition to editing tools, ONLYOFFICE offers a shared workspace where teams can organize documents into rooms and manage access permissions securely.

Support for popular Microsoft Office formats makes it easier to exchange files with clients, partners, and other external stakeholders without compatibility concerns. The World Food Travel Association, for example, uses ONLYOFFICE to collaborate effectively across multiple time zones and engage volunteers in its projects.

CREATE FREE CLOUD

Pros: Collaborative editing, Office format compatibility, flexible sharing permissions, cloud or self-hosted deployment.

Cons: Project scheduling and team messaging require separate tools.

Pricing: The Cloud Startup plan is free. The Business plan is currently available at a rate of $20 per admin per month.

Best for: Teams working with Office documents and businesses regularly collaborating with external partners.

2. Google Workspace

Google Workspace brings Docs, Sheets, Slides, Gmail, Drive, and Calendar into one connected environment. Several colleagues can edit the same document, discuss changes in comments, and access the latest version without exchanging email attachments.

The applications work primarily in a browser, although complex Microsoft Office files may need formatting adjustments when opened in Google’s editors.

Pros: Real-time collaboration, simple file sharing, and integration across Google services.

Cons: Advanced spreadsheet features and complex Office formatting may not transfer perfectly between applications.

Pricing: Business Starter costs $7 per user per month with annual commitment; Business Standard costs $14.

Best for: Teams that regularly collaborate on documents and already use Google’s business applications.

3. Microsoft 365

Microsoft 365 combines Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook with online storage and collaboration services. Its desktop applications remain useful for detailed spreadsheets, complex documents, and presentations requiring precise formatting.

Employees can work locally or online and share files through Microsoft cloud services. Businesses should review the available subscriptions carefully, as desktop applications, Teams, and other services are not included in every package.

Pros: Advanced Office applications, desktop and online editing, and integrated business services.

Cons: Multiple subscription options and additional administration for larger deployments.

Pricing: Business Basic with Teams starts at $7 per user per month with annual billing. Business Standard, which includes desktop Office applications, starts at $14.

Best for: Businesses already using Microsoft products and teams working extensively with Office documents.

Project and task management

A task manager gives everyone a clearer picture of their responsibilities, upcoming deadlines, and the progress of shared projects.

4. Asana

Asana helps teams coordinate assignments through lists, boards, calendars, and timelines. Tasks can include deadlines, comments, attachments, and dependencies, making it easier to follow work involving several contributors.

Marketing and operations teams can use Asana to keep projects moving between departments, with additional reporting and resource management features available on higher-tier plans.

Pros: Clear task ownership, multiple project views, and cross-team coordination.

Cons: Portfolio and workload management require more expensive subscriptions.

Pricing: Personal is free for up to two users. Starter costs $10.99 per user per month with annual billing.

Best for: Teams managing projects with multiple contributors and approval stages.

5. Trello

Trello uses visual boards to organize work into lists and cards. An editorial team, for example, can move articles from writing to editing and publication, with deadlines, checklists, and supporting files attached to each card.

The interface is easy to learn and works particularly well for projects with clearly defined stages. More complicated schedules and task dependencies may call for additional project management features.

Pros: Easy setup, customizable boards, and visual progress tracking.

Cons: Limited advanced scheduling and reporting compared with more comprehensive project management platforms.

Image source: Trello

Pricing: A free plan is available. Standard costs $5 per user per month with annual billing; Premium costs $10.

Best for: Small teams, editorial calendars, and straightforward project workflows.

6. ClickUp

ClickUp combines task management with documents, dashboards, time tracking, and workflow automation. Agencies can use it to organize several client projects, keeping assignments and supporting materials in the same workspace.

Teams can customize project views and task statuses, but that flexibility also requires some planning. An overly complicated workspace may become difficult to maintain as more people and projects are added.

Pros: Customizable workflows, multiple project views, and integrated documents.

Cons: More configuration is needed than with a simple task management app.

Pricing: Free Forever is available. Unlimited starts at $7 per user per month with annual billing.

Best for: Agencies and growing teams managing several projects simultaneously.

Team communication

Team communication apps provide a shared space for everyday discussions, project updates, and quick questions that do not require a formal meeting.

7. Slack

Slack keeps conversations organized in channels dedicated to projects, departments, or specific topics. Employees can share files, exchange messages, and receive updates from connected business applications.

Its extensive integrations make it convenient for teams working across several platforms. However, important decisions can get lost when discussions are spread across too many channels.

Pros: Organized messaging, integrations with other tools, and collaboration with external partners.

Cons: Excessive notifications and lengthy message threads can make information harder to follow.

Image source: Slack

Pricing: A free plan is available. Pro costs $7.25 per active user per month with annual billing.

Best for: Remote teams and businesses using several specialized applications.

8. Microsoft Teams

Microsoft Teams brings messaging, meetings, and file sharing together. Employees using Microsoft 365 can discuss projects in dedicated channels and open shared Office documents directly from their workspace.

Teams is a convenient choice for organizations already working within Microsoft’s ecosystem. As the number of projects grows, consistent channel organization becomes important for keeping conversations and documents easy to find.

Pros: Integrated messaging, meetings, and document collaboration.

Cons: Conversations and files can become scattered across chats and channels.

Pricing: Teams Essentials starts at $4 per user per month with annual billing. Teams is also included in eligible Microsoft 365 subscriptions.

Best for: Organizations using Microsoft 365 and teams combining office-based and remote work.

9. Mattermost

Mattermost provides channel-based messaging and file sharing, with the option to run the platform on an organization’s own infrastructure.

Its deployment flexibility appeals to development teams and IT departments that need greater control over their communication environment. Self-hosting, however, requires technical resources for installation, updates, and maintenance.

Pros: Flexible hosting, organized communication, and support for technical workflows.

Cons: Self-hosted deployments require ongoing administration.

Pricing: A free, open-source Team Edition is available for self-hosting. Commercial Professional and Enterprise plans require a sales quotation.

Best for: Development teams, IT departments, and organizations with specific hosting requirements.

Video conferencing and online meetings

Video conferencing tools are used for everything from short team calls to training sessions and virtual events. Meeting duration, participant limits, and compatibility with existing calendars are worth checking before choosing a platform.

10. Zoom

Zoom supports video meetings, webinars, and virtual workshops. Screen sharing and breakout rooms let participants present information, hold smaller discussions, and return to the main meeting afterward.

Zoom Workplace also includes messaging and collaborative features. Businesses planning longer sessions should consider a paid plan, as free group meetings have a time limit.

Pros: Flexible meeting formats, breakout rooms, and screen sharing.

Cons: Free group meetings are limited to 40 minutes.

Image source: Zoom

Pricing: Zoom Workplace Basic is free. Pro is listed at $15.99 per user per month with monthly billing.

Best for: Client meetings, online training, and virtual workshops.

11. Google Meet

Google Meet works with Google Calendar and other Workspace applications, making it easy to schedule and join meetings directly from a browser. Participants can share their screens and join calls without installing additional desktop software.

The free version covers basic meetings, while recording and other advanced features are available through eligible Google Workspace subscriptions.

Pros: Browser-based access and integration with Google Calendar.

Cons: Free group meetings are limited to 60 minutes.

Pricing: A free version is available. Additional business features are included in eligible Google Workspace plans, starting at $7 per user per month with annual commitment.

Best for: Small businesses and teams already using Google Workspace.

12. Webex

Webex by Cisco offers video meetings, messaging, and screen sharing. Businesses with compatible Cisco meeting room equipment can connect employees attending from the office with colleagues joining remotely.

The platform also supports more extensive communication requirements, although its different meeting and calling products have separate licensing options.

Pros: Hybrid meeting support and integration with Cisco equipment.

Cons: Selecting the appropriate plan requires comparing different communication and meeting products.

Pricing: Webex Free supports meetings lasting up to 40 minutes. Webex Meet starts at $12 per user per month with annual billing.

Best for: Hybrid organizations and businesses using Cisco collaboration systems.

Cloud storage and file sharing

Cloud storage keeps documents and other business files accessible across devices. When comparing services, consider how files are synchronized, who can access them, and whether storage is already included in your office software.

13. Google Drive

Google Drive stores documents, spreadsheets, images, and other files online. Employees can share folders, manage access permissions, and open compatible files directly in Google Workspace.

Business subscriptions also provide shared drives, allowing project files to remain available to the team rather than being stored exclusively in an individual employee’s account.

Pros: Easy sharing, collaborative editing, and shared team storage.

Cons: Storage is shared across Google services, and external sharing permissions need careful management.

Pricing: Personal accounts include 15 GB of free storage. Workspace Business Starter provides 30 GB of pooled storage per user for $7 per user per month with annual commitment.

Best for: Teams working extensively with Google documents.

14. Dropbox

Dropbox synchronizes files across devices and makes it easy to share materials with colleagues or clients. Its desktop application works with familiar folders, so employees can continue managing files without changing how they normally navigate their computers.

Creative agencies can use Dropbox to exchange large design files and media assets, although editing Office documents and managing complex projects may require separate applications.

Pros: Cross-device synchronization, convenient file sharing, and large file transfers.

Cons: Limited free storage and fewer native office editing features than dedicated office suites.

Pricing: Dropbox Basic is free with 2 GB of storage. Standard costs $15 per user per month.

Best for: Creative agencies and businesses regularly exchanging large files.

15. OneDrive

OneDrive integrates cloud storage with Windows and Microsoft 365. Employees can synchronize files across devices, share documents, and open compatible files in Office applications.

OneDrive is generally used for files associated with individual employees, while SharePoint provides shared document libraries for departments and project teams.

Pros: Windows integration, file synchronization, and Office collaboration.

Cons: Teams need clear guidelines for organizing files between OneDrive and SharePoint.

Pricing: OneDrive is included in Microsoft 365 Business Basic, starting at $7 per user per month with annual billing and providing 1 TB of cloud storage per user.

Best for: Businesses already using Microsoft 365.

Time management, scheduling and time tracking

Time management apps help businesses record working hours, review project costs, and arrange appointments. The tools below cover two distinct needs: tracking time spent on work and finding suitable meeting times.

16. Toggl Track

Toggl Track records time spent on tasks, projects, and client assignments. Employees can start a timer or enter hours manually, while reports help businesses review billable work and prepare more accurate project estimates.

Pros: Simple time recording, project reports, and billable time tracking.

Cons: Advanced reporting and team management features require paid subscriptions.

Image source: Toggle Track

Pricing: A free plan is available. Starter costs $9 per user per month with annual billing.

Best for: Freelancers, consultants, and agencies tracking billable hours.

17. Clockify

Clockify combines time tracking with timesheets and project reporting. Employees record their hours against individual activities, giving managers a clearer picture of the time spent on different assignments.

Paid plans extend these features with invoicing, timesheet approvals, and additional administration options.

Pros: Free time tracking, timesheets, and project reports.

Cons: Invoicing and timesheet approvals require paid plans.

Pricing: A free plan is available. Basic starts at $3.99 per seat per month with annual billing.

Best for: Small businesses and teams that need detailed timesheets.

18. Calendly

Calendly takes the back-and-forth out of appointment scheduling. Users share a booking link, and clients or colleagues select a time based on their availability and connected calendars.

Recruiters, consultants, and sales teams can use it to arrange interviews, consultations, and product demonstrations. Paid subscriptions add more advanced scheduling options for teams.

Pros: Automated booking, calendar integrations, and meeting reminders.

Cons: Multiple event types and advanced team scheduling require a paid plan.

Pricing: A free plan is available. Standard starts at $10 per seat per month with annual billing.

Best for: Recruiters, consultants, and sales teams arranging frequent appointments.

AI productivity tools

AI tools can assist with writing, research, and information retrieval. Some work as standalone assistants, while others use content already stored in an organization’s collaborative workspace.

19. ChatGPT

ChatGPT can help employees prepare content outlines, summarize reports, analyze data, and draft internal documents. Its range of capabilities makes it useful across different departments, from marketing and research to software development.

AI-generated information should still be checked before being used in professional materials. Businesses also need appropriate privacy settings when working with confidential information.

Pros: Assistance with writing, research, analysis, and document preparation.

Cons: Generated information requires verification, and confidential data needs appropriate privacy controls.

Pricing: A free plan is available. ChatGPT Business Standard seats start at $20 per user per month with annual billing.

Best for: Marketing teams, researchers, analysts, and other knowledge workers.

20. Notion AI

Notion AI adds AI-assisted writing, summarization, and search to Notion’s collaborative workspace. Teams can retrieve information from their existing project plans, meeting notes, and internal documentation without switching to another application.

Its value depends on the quality of the material stored in Notion, making consistent documentation important for reliable information retrieval.

Pros: Document summarization, knowledge retrieval, and AI assistance within an existing workspace.

Cons: An organized knowledge base and an eligible subscription are needed to make full use of its capabilities.

Image source: Notion

Pricing: Notion offers a free plan with limited AI access. Its Business subscription includes expanded AI capabilities, with pricing depending on the billing option and region.

Best for: Teams managing internal documentation and shared knowledge in Notion.

How to choose a cloud-based productivity app

Begin with the tasks that take up most of your team’s time. A business handling contracts and reports may need an office suite with reliable document compatibility, while an agency managing several client projects may benefit more from dedicated task management software.

Check your existing subscriptions before adding new applications. Google Workspace and Microsoft 365, for example, already include document editing, storage, and video conferencing. You may not need a separate tool for every activity.

Costs should be assessed across the whole team, including storage, administration features, and access for external collaborators. Review security and sharing permissions as well, particularly when employees work with confidential documents.

Before committing to a platform, test it with a real project. Involve the employees who will use it regularly and see how easily they can find information, complete assignments, and work together.

Conclusion

Cloud-based productivity apps help teams manage documents, projects, communication, and other everyday activities. Choosing the right combination starts with understanding your team’s needs and making use of the software you already have.

A few well-chosen tools can provide everything a team needs without adding unnecessary complexity or extra subscriptions.

contentHtml:
Cross-border document collaboration involving Mainland China has long meant a frustrating trade-off: painful latency, throttled bandwidth, and tough questions about where your data actually lives. Now, ONLYOFFICE and Cloud Systems Asia (CSA) are changing that with a Hong Kong-hosted FileCloud + ONLYOFFICE solution built to deliver secure, high-performance collaboration for global teams. Here’s how this partnership removes the performance barriers and keeps your data firmly within a trusted regional perimeter.

ONLYOFFICE & FileCloud: solving the cross-border collaboration challenge

Managing document collaboration that involves Mainland China has always been tricky. Standard methods for overseas users accessing files stored in Mainland China often lead to severe latency and bandwidth throttling, which slows teams down and frustrates everyone involved.

CSA solves this with a smart, purpose-built approach. By hosting a complete Microsoft 365-like solution in Hong Kong that combines FileCloud and ONLYOFFICE, CSA creates a high-performance regional bridge.

Here’s what that means in practice:

  • For Mainland China users: smooth, reliable connections to global teams.
  • For worldwide users: low-latency, real-time access from anywhere.
  • For everyone: secure file storage, seamless sharing, and online document co-authoring in one turnkey package.

This Hong Kong-hosted architecture delivers the key functionality enterprises expect, while removing the performance barriers that usually stand in the way of true cross-border teamwork.

Data sovereignty and on-premises security

Security and data control are top priorities for any enterprise, and this solution is built with both in mind. Some organizations have raised concerns about servers hosted in the US, which is a valid consideration when data residency and compliance are at stake.

CSA addresses this head-on. The complete solution keeps all files localized on on-premises infrastructure, giving organizations full control over where their data lives. CSA can build and host both ONLYOFFICE and FileCloud in Hong Kong, delivering a seamless collaboration platform that connects users in Mainland China with teams around the world, all while keeping data firmly within a trusted regional perimeter.

ONLYOFFICE welcomes Cloud Systems Asia as a new partner

We’re excited to announce a new partnership between ONLYOFFICE and Cloud Systems Asia Limited (CSA). Together, we’re making secure, high-performance document collaboration easier for global organizations, especially those working across borders with teams in Mainland China.

Cloud Systems Asia Limited is a Hong Kong-based value-added distributor that specializes in enterprise-grade file collaboration solutions. Through a strong network of channel partners, resellers, and system integrators, CSA serves organizations across corporate, government, retail, finance, healthcare, and manufacturing sectors.

This partnership matters because it brings ONLYOFFICE’s powerful editing capabilities together with CSA’s deep regional expertise. The result is a practical, ready-to-deploy solution for enterprises that need reliable collaboration without compromising on speed or security.

FileCloud + ONLYOFFICE: editing made seamless

One of the key products in CSA’s portfolio is FileCloud, and it works beautifully with ONLYOFFICE. This integration lets users open, view, edit, and co-author office documents directly within the FileCloud web interface – no need to leave the browser or switch between apps.

Your teams can work with all the popular formats they rely on every day, including text documents (.docx), spreadsheets (.xlsx), and presentations (.pptx).

Everything happens in one place, keeping workflows smooth and productivity high. It’s a straightforward way to give employees the familiar office tools they expect, fully integrated into the platform they already use.

Get started with CSA and ONLYOFFICE

This partnership opens up real opportunities for enterprises and channel partners alike. Whether you’re a global organization looking to streamline cross-border collaboration or a reseller seeking a proven, scalable solution to offer your clients, the CSA FileCloud + ONLYOFFICE combination delivers.

Ready to bring reliable, secure, high-performance document collaboration to your teams? Connect with Cloud Systems Asia to explore how this solution can work for your organization.

We look forward to what ONLYOFFICE and CSA will achieve together, and to helping enterprises everywhere collaborate without limits.

contentHtml:
Microsoft is ending support for key on-premises products this year, including Office Online Server, SharePoint Server 2016 and 2019, and Exchange Server, while standalone SharePoint plans are also being phased out. For many organizations, that sounds like a forced and disruptive migration, but in most cases, there’s a simpler path: keep your files and systems where they are, and just change the editing tool without disrupting daily work.

The Microsoft 365 end-of-support situation

The deadlines are fixed, and they arrive quickly. Office Online Server, the product that powers browser-based document editing on your own infrastructure, retires in December with no on-premises successor. SharePoint Server 2016 and 2019 lost support in July. Exchange Server support has also lapsed.

The pattern is clear: the only path Microsoft is offering leads to its cloud. For organizations in finance, healthcare, government, and other regulated sectors, that’s not always a viable option. Data sovereignty rules, compliance mandates, and internal governance policies often require documents to stay on infrastructure you control.

So the question isn’t whether to act, the timeline decides that for you. The question is how to act without triggering the disruption everyone dreads.

Why full migration is often unnecessary

Most of the fear around leaving Microsoft 365 rests on a single assumption: that moving on means a complete migration. Files relocated. Folder structures rebuilt. Permissions reconfigured. Workflows redesigned from scratch.

That assumption is wrong for the majority of teams.

Instead of moving anything, you connect a new editing suite to the platform you already use. Your files stay put. Your folder hierarchy, access controls, and permissions remain untouched. Your team keeps working with the same DOCX, XLSX, and PPTX files they’ve always used. The only thing that changes is the editing layer.

Think of it as a connection plan, not a migration plan. There’s no single moment where everything stops while IT relocates files. This distinction matters most right now, because it gives you a way to keep operating on your own infrastructure, on your own terms, and on your own timeline.

What ONLYOFFICE is and how it connects

ONLYOFFICE is a comprehensive office suite covering documents, spreadsheets, presentations, and PDFs, all built around the Office Open XML standard. DOCX, XLSX, and PPTX are its native working formats, not imports that get converted behind the scenes.

The source code is published under an open-source license, so anyone can inspect and audit exactly what the software does with their data. For organizations with strict data governance requirements, that transparency is a meaningful advantage.

You deploy ONLYOFFICE on your own servers or in the cloud – whichever fits your situation – and connect it to your existing storage or collaboration platform. Ready-made connectors are available for dozens of platforms, including SharePoint, Confluence, ownCloud, Odoo, etc., with an open API for everything else.

Here’s how it works in practice with SharePoint:

Install the connector, and a new “Edit in ONLYOFFICE” option appears in your document library. Click it, and the file opens in the ONLYOFFICE editor right in your browser. Edit, save, and the file returns to SharePoint. No file transfer, no background format conversion. Your IT team configures the connection once, and after that, it’s invisible to the people using it. For teams currently running Office Online Server on SharePoint, this is a direct replacement.

Key features your team will use every day

Once connected, the first thing people notice is how familiar the interface feels. The toolbar layout, tab structure, and formatting options follow the conventions your team already knows from Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. There’s no steep learning curve.

These are full-featured editors, not stripped-down viewers:

  • Document editor: styles, tables, headers and footers, table of contents, mail merge, and document comparison.
